summary: Safely associate rooms with homes by home_id, gated behind a migration flag. Legacy rooms are migrated explicitly and idempotently into a default home; all per-room state and links are preserved. Acceptance criteria are validated by detailed migration and regression tests, recovery documentation, and careful flag-based control. This work is high-risk and requires thorough human and test verification, with no UI or API changes in this slice.
steps: Document current room and home mapping, including all context-key logic and compatibility, based on app/project.py and app/store.py.
Update models so every room gets a home association by home_id, with ownership based on IDs (not names). Duplicate room names are supported; context keys remain compatible with previous flows.

Implement a safe, idempotent migration script in migrations/migration_0001_room_home.py: create a default home, migrate all legacy rooms, preserve existing state/context/links, log each action, allow recovery from interruptions, assign only when the migration flag is set.
Define and enforce decora-room-home-migration in app/flags.py, defaulting to off. Migration must only run when this flag is explicitly enabled. No implicit migration on import or startup.

Update MCP server (mcp_servers/decor_design.py) code as needed to guarantee that all project and room MCP routes/resources work identically for both pre- and post-migration data, using correct home/room isolation logic. Regression paths for context keys and project resources must remain compatible.

Write exhaustive migration and compatibility tests in tests/migrations/test_migration_0001_room_home.py. Include: legacy to migrated state, round trip, repeat runs, simulated interruptions, link and resource preservation, flag-off and flag-on regression. (Partition into multiple tasks to keep at most six test functions per task.)

Document the full migration, rollback, and data recovery plan in docs/room_home_migration.md, including all constraints, flag control, step breakdowns, recovery instructions, idempotency, edge-case analysis, and necessary manual steps for human review. Reference observed code/behavior.

Provision and gate all new migration/home logic and tests with the required decora-room-home-migration flag, referencing the mandatory key (must match policy) and enforcing at every code and test entry point.

flag_rationale: High-risk migration of core project and room data; flag required to permit safe, stepwise, manually approved rollout, as required by policy. No frontline or user-exposed changes occur until flagged and reviewed. Migration code is strictly isolated.
migration_plan:
- Migration runs only when the decora-room-home-migration flag is explicitly set (never on startup or import).
- Script establishes a default home (idempotently/uniquely).
- Each legacy room is assigned to the default home, with all associated per-room state and external/context key links preserved.
- Logs every migration step for recoverability; no original data is destroyed until explicit human verification/approval.
- Migration is idempotent and safe to repeat—previously migrated rooms skipped (never duplicated or mixed).
- Partial failures: migration records stepwise status, can be resumed or recovered manually by reviewing logs/partial output.
- Rollback: no automatic rollback; on error, require manual restore from backup or data review per the doc. All migration/rollback guidance is documented in docs/room_home_migration.md.
- All pre- and post-migration codepaths for context keys/room/home lookup are preserved and tested for regression compatibility.
- Thorough test suite in tests/migrations, run in isolation, with coverage for all acceptance, edge cases, repeated executions, interrupted states, and flag-off/on compatibility.
- Human review and approval are mandatory before migration is executed in non-test environments.
risks: Possible edge cases with legacy or malformed room/project data affecting migration or mixing state.
Context key or external/project link breakage if isolation is not comprehensive.
Backup/restore must be handled with great care; improper human intervention could corrupt mapping.
Migration code must never auto-execute; human and test review mandatory before launch.
assumptions: Default home is uniquely/clearly named and discoverable.
All per-room/project state is stored in isolatable, discoverable structures. No untracked/sideband state.
All MCP and context key features are represented in observable test regressions and project briefs.
